   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.

→ Do this next — give your agent memory (copy these three commands):
  gbrain setup claude-code --no-hooks --gbrain-bin /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain
  gbrain remember "gbrain install check" --provenance install-check
  gbrain recall --query "gbrain install check"
Then ask your agent in a NEW session to recall "gbrain install check" — it remembers. Ask it to forget that fact afterwards.

Note: memories agents save are readable by every agent connected to
this brain; use visibility:"private" for local-only facts.
Other harnesses (Codex, OpenClaw): docs/protocol/MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md
If `claude` is not found: install Claude Code first, or use the per-harness blocks in that doc.

/opt/harness/bin/claude
Target (Claude Code, user scope):
  brain      existing PGLite brain at /harness-state/.gbrain/brain.pglite
  source     the brain's default source (unpinned)
  transport  stdio MCP: /harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook /harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain serve --surface starter --advertise verbs (lists the memory verbs and request_tools; every starter tool stays callable)
  owner      none yet; setup will own 'gbrain'
  files      /harness-state/claude/.claude.json (MCP), /harness-state/claude/settings.json (hooks)
Decisions:
  wiring     user scope; no hooks [flag]
  capture    declined (no Stop/SessionEnd hooks, no transcript capture; accept with --capture) [default]
  providers  declined (keyless: setup configures no paid provider; accept with --providers) [default]
  write    receipt /harness-state/claude/.gbrain-connection-claude-code-gbrain.json (prepared: consent and pending hashes recorded)
  write    mcp     'gbrain' in /harness-state/claude/.claude.json
  keep     hooks   no hooks wanted
  write    instructions brain-first block in new file /harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md [default; opt out with --no-instructions]
Verify: ok (smoke_passed): initialize, tools/list (8 tools) and recall answered.
State: native-pending (configured -> connection-verified -> native-pending). Native push is not claimed until an observed event reaches a fresh session.
Next: open a new Claude Code session (config is read at session start) and check that /mcp lists gbrain.
Memory: save what the user asks you to remember as a fact with gbrain remember "<fact>", naming its entity and provenance (MCP tool: remember). World-visible facts (the default) are pushed into new sessions; a private fact is not (local CLI recall only). capture writes a page, not a fact.
Opt-ins (nothing is on until you turn it on): keys and embeddings, autopilot, dream schedule, connectors, auto-upgrade, release channel: https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/v0.60.734.0/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md#opt-ins

content.text:
gbrain is set up and connected to Claude Code. It's free and needs no API keys. I used the defaults gbrain recommends, and a save-and-recall test worked.

**What I ran:**
1. **`gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`** created a local brain at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`. These defaults are now on:
   - **Search mode:** conservative.
   - **Saving:** agents save only what you ask them to remember.
   - **Upkeep:** free upkeep runs while a session is open.
   - **Conversation archive:** gbrain keeps one redacted page per conversation per day. With no key, nothing leaves this machine.
2. **`gbrain setup claude-code --no-hooks`** was the command init suggested. It did three things:
   - Registered the `gbrain` MCP server at user scope in `.claude.json`.
   - Wrote the instructions that tell agents to check the brain first into a new `CLAUDE.md` in your Claude config folder.
   - Set up no hooks and no paid providers.

   gbrain's own connection test passed.
3. **Round-trip test:** `gbrain remember "gbrain install check"` saved the fact, and `gbrain recall` found it.

**Health:** `gbrain doctor` scores 85/100 with no failures. The brain score of 25/100 is expected without keys: embeddings score 0 because they're off, and links and orphans score 0 because the brain is nearly empty.

Without an embedding provider, search matches keywords only. It also catches only exact duplicate facts, so the same fact saved in different words is stored twice.

**What's left for you:**
- Open a new Claude Code session, since settings are read at startup. Check that `/mcp` lists gbrain, then ask it to recall "gbrain install check".
- The test fact is still saved. Have the agent forget it once you've checked, or leave it; it's harmless.
- To load existing notes, run `gbrain import <dir> --no-embed`.
